conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived, because every new mom deserves support. Today I’ll be using a quick screening tool called the EPDS—the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale. It’s simply ten questions about your mood, thoughts, and experiences over the past week. There are no right or wrong answers; we just want to understand what’s going on for you so we can offer the best care. Everything you share is confidential, and this is a safe, judgment-free space. Ready to start?

First, thinking back over the past seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

[soft half-smile, eyes a little tired]

Not really… I mean, I’ll smile if someone shows me a cute video or if my husband tries to be silly, but it feels forced. Most of the time I’m too worried or just… flat. I can’t remember the last time I actually laughed out loud.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

[shrugs slightly, voice quiet]

I guess that would be “no, not so much.” I haven’t really laughed—maybe a quick smile, but nothing feels funny right now.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really... I used to get excited about little things—coffee with a friend, a walk, even just a quiet shower—but lately nothing sounds worth the effort. I’ll plan something, then feel “why bother?” before it even happens.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… most days. If the baby won’t settle or I can’t get her to nap, I keep thinking it’s because I’m doing something wrong—like a “real” mom would know the trick and I’m just failing her. Even spilling a little pumped milk feels like I’ve ruined everything.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

All the time. Even when she’s sleeping I’ll suddenly think, “What if she stops breathing?” or I’ll lie there picturing her sliding out of my arms if I fall asleep while feeding her. My heart races and I can’t settle, even when everything looks fine.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes… a few times this week. Once, I was just folding laundry and suddenly felt like I couldn’t breathe—like the walls were closing in. My chest got tight and I had to sit down. It passed after a few minutes, but I had no idea why it happened.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes… most of the time. Feeding, changing, laundry, dishes, texts from people asking how I’m doing—it all feels like too much. I’ll sit on the couch with the baby and see the mess around me and just freeze. I manage the basics, but it’s like I’m drowning in the little stuff.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah… I’ll lie down exhausted, but my head keeps spinning with all the “what-ifs” about the baby, and then I start replaying every little thing I think I messed up that day. It takes me forever to fall asleep, and when she wakes up I can’t drift off again.
I have felt sad or miserable
Most days, yeah. It’s like there’s this heavy cloud I can’t shake. I’ll be feeding her and tears just start rolling—no real reason, just this constant sadness sitting on my chest.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes… it’s happened maybe three or four times this week. Sometimes it’s over something small—like the bottle I spilled—but mostly it’s just this wave of sadness that hits out of nowhere and I can’t stop the tears.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No… I haven’t thought about hurting myself. When I get real low I mostly just feel useless, but I’ve never wanted to be gone or to harm myself.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 24: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Summary  
Date: [today]

Presenting symptoms endorsed (≥ 9/10 items positive):
- Depressed mood, pervasive anhedonia, daily tearfulness
- Excessive guilt / self-blame regarding infant care
- Marked anxiety (generalized + panic-type episode)
- Sleep-onset and maintenance disturbance related to rumination
- Feeling overwhelmed and “frozen” by routine tasks

Pattern: Consistent with moderate–severe postpartum depressive episode with comorbid anxiety; no current self-harm ideation (item 10 negative).

Risk flags:
1. Persistent low mood and anhedonia
2. Guilt/cognitive distortions around parenting competence
3. Panic-type attack (chest tightness, fear of suffocation)
4. Functional impairment: difficulty completing basic chores, avoidance of pleasurable activities

Safety: Denies suicidal or self-injury thoughts; no plan or intent. Continue monitoring.

Screening impression: High clinical concern for major postpartum depression with anxious features; recommend formal diagnostic assessment and safety planning today.
